constraints: New private workspace package packages/agent-tools (@exharness/agent-tools, type module, node >=20) with no runtime npm dependencies; it imports Core from ../../core-harness/src/index.js and the BB-096 adapters from ../../agentic-system/src/index.js, the same relative convention packages/agentic-system uses.

Every process is started with spawn and an argument array and shell:false; on win32 an npm .cmd/.ps1 shim is resolved to its JavaScript entry and run with process.execPath, and cmd.exe/powershell are never used.

Every test in the package is titled with its criterion prefix (AT1..AT4 followed by a space), declares { timeout: 60000 }, uses only fake CLIs and temp git repositories, and removes worktrees and temp dirs in finally blocks.

Root package.json gains test:agent-tools (node --test packages/agent-tools/test/*.test.js) appended to the test script, and smoke:agent-tools (node packages/agent-tools/bin/exharness-agent.mjs smoke) which is not part of test or verify.
Adapters are not a sandbox; docs must state that live runs execute with the user's CLI permissions inside a temp worktree only and point isolation to BB-067.
Research only in this lane: no product source edits, no self-issued readiness or fabricated Jev judgment.
invariants: Only a candidate whose declared verifications all PASS at its exact commit can be promoted; the agent exit status or message never contributes to acceptance.

ExHarness launches each agent with cwd at a worktree under os.tmpdir(); its own git operations preserve the source repository HEAD, branch refs and working tree. The CLI is unsandboxed and may access paths outside that worktree under the user account.
No process is started through a shell, and every agent invocation is bounded by a timeout that kills its process tree.
User CLI configuration and credentials are never read or written by the adapters.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Files: packages/agent-tools/{package.json, src/index.js, src/tool-adapters.js, src/process-runner.js, src/supervisor.js, bin/exharness-agent.mjs, test/agent-tools.test.js, test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs}. Root exports: defineAgentTool, codexTool, kiroTool, agyTool, runAgentInvocation, createSupervisedAgentStrategy, runSupervisedTask, AgentTaskStatus.

D2 — AGENT_TOOL_ADAPTER_V1 = { id, command, prefixArgs = [], versionArgs, buildInvocation({ prompt, resume, model, permissionProfile, logFile, timeoutMs }) -> { args, stdin } where resume is null for a first invocation or { sessionRef } (sessionRef may be null) for a resume, parseResult({ exitCode, stdout, stderr }) -> { claimedSuccess, finalMessage, sessionRef }, where sessionRef is required only for codex and is null for kiro/agy }. defineAgentTool(base, { command, prefixArgs }) replaces the resolved launch tuple (command plus prefixArgs) atomically while preserving base.buildInvocation and base.parseResult; a fake .mjs uses command = process.execPath and prefixArgs = [absoluteFakePath].

D3 — Invocations. Flags and values present in the executed probe help output: codex exec --json/--sandbox workspace-write|danger-full-access/--skip-git-repo-check/--model, codex exec resume [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT] with `-` reading the prompt from stdin, plus --json; kiro-cli chat --no-interactive/--trust-tools=<list> (help example fs_read,fs_write)/--trust-all-tools/--resume/--model; agy --print/--continue/--mode accept-edits/--dangerously-skip-permissions/--log-file/--print-timeout/--model. codex first = [exec, --json, --skip-git-repo-check, --sandbox, workspace-write (FULL_AUTO: danger-full-access), (--model m), -] with the prompt on stdin; resume = [exec, resume, <resume.sessionRef>, --json, -] with the prompt on stdin, where sessionRef is the thread_id/session_id that codex parseResult extracted from the --json stream of the first invocation; when resume.sessionRef is null the codex adapter builds a fresh first invocation instead. kiro ignores sessionRef because --resume is scoped to the worktree cwd by its help text. kiro first = [chat, --no-interactive, --trust-tools=fs_read,fs_write (FULL_AUTO: --trust-all-tools), (--model m), <prompt>]; resume inserts --resume after chat. The WORKSPACE_EDIT list uses only the two tool names shown in the kiro help example; shell execution requires FULL_AUTO. agy first = [--print, <prompt>, --mode, accept-edits (FULL_AUTO: --dangerously-skip-permissions instead of --mode), --print-timeout, <timeoutSeconds>s, (--model m), --log-file, <path>]; resume inserts --continue. The process cwd is always the worktree root. agy --continue resumes the most recent conversation for the active workspace cwd according to the official Antigravity CLI resume documentation (workspace-keyed cache); the worktree path is unique per task run, and the supervisor passes the complete task plus bounded feedback on every attempt. agy ignores sessionRef because --continue resolves by cwd; no adapter reads the CLI cache. agy help prints the --print-timeout default as 5m0s, so timeoutSeconds is a positive integer rounded up from timeoutMs and formatted as a seconds duration. D3 is the frozen argv contract for codex-cli 0.158.0, kiro-cli-chat 2.24.1 and agy 1.1.1; no CLI flag selection is delegated to the Worker.

D4 — runAgentInvocation(tool, request, { cwd, env = {}, timeoutMs = 600000, maxOutputBytes = 1048576 }) spawns tool.command with [...prefixArgs, ...args] and process.env overlaid with env, writes stdin when present, streams stdout/stderr through incremental SHA-256 digests while retaining at most maxOutputBytes per stream (recording truncation), and on timeout kills the process tree (POSIX: detached + process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL"); win32: spawn taskkill with ["/pid", String(pid), "/T", "/F"] and shell:false, then wait for both taskkill and the tool to exit). It returns { exitCode, signal, timedOut, durationMs, stdout, stderr, stdoutSha256, stderrSha256, truncated }. A missing executable (ENOENT) returns { status: "TOOL_UNAVAILABLE", exitCode: null, timedOut: false } without throwing. The supervisor applies tool.parseResult to normal exit results; it never treats parsed claimedSuccess as verification. resolveExecutable(command, { platform, pathEnv }) searches PATH; on win32, when the hit is an npm shim (<name>.cmd or <name>.ps1 next to node_modules), it returns { command: process.execPath, prefixArgs: [<absolute JS entry parsed from the shim target>] }; native .exe hits are returned unchanged. An explicit absolute .mjs/.js --command path, including the fake CLI fixture, resolves to { command: process.execPath, prefixArgs: [that path] }; this resolution precedes PATH lookup.

D5 — Supervisor: runSupervisedTask({ tool, task, model = null, maxAttempts = 3, timeoutMs, maxFeedbackChars = 8000, permissionProfile, env = {}, eventSinks = [], tracer = null }) validates AGENT_TASK_V1, creates a unique worktreeRoot under os.tmpdir(), and obtains BB-096 createLocalGitWorkspace({ repositoryRoot: task.repositoryRoot, baseRevision: task.baseRevision, worktreeRoot }). It probes tool.versionArgs from that worktree with a bounded shell-free invocation to set toolVersion. It creates agentToolEnvironment with observe delegated to workspace.observe and act({ candidate, action }) defined in D6; the tool process and git commit both occur inside Core AVOCapability.ACT, so the Core effect journal records intent before mutation. The BB-096 workspace owns worktree creation/head/disposal and BB-096 createLocalCommandVerifier owns revision-bound verification; agentToolEnvironment owns this task-specific ACT because its action must include the external agent process. It creates one verifier per declared verification (root = workspace.root, claim = `agent-task.${name}`, requireUnchangedTree true). It composes createHarness({ strategy: createSupervisedAgentStrategy(...), environment: agentToolEnvironment, verifiers, verificationPolicy: { requirements: one { claim } per declared verifier }, variationPolicy: { maxCapabilityCalls: maxAttempts * (verifiers.length + 3) }, objective, eventSinks, tracer }), chooses a fresh sessionId, calls harness.start({ sessionId, work: { id: task.id, prompt: task.prompt }, seedCandidate: { id: task.id, version: task.baseRevision } }), and runs one harness.vary(sessionId). It disposes the worktree in finally.

D6 — Attempt loop: strategy.run({ input, invoke }) holds currentCandidate = input.candidate and builds attempt 1 prompt = task.prompt; each later prompt appends a block beginning exactly `ExHarness verification failed:` with each failing verifier name, status, reason and bounded output tail (total <= maxFeedbackChars). For index 1..maxAttempts it invokes AVOCapability.ACT once with { kind: "RUN_AGENT_TOOL", attemptIndex: index, prompt, resume: prior sessionRef or null }; attemptIndex makes the Core action-effect key unique even after a no-change attempt. agentToolEnvironment.act asserts `git rev-parse HEAD` at workspace.root equals candidate.version, calls runAgentInvocation with cwd = workspace.root, parses only telemetry, and, if the agent made descendant commits, folds them with `git reset --soft <candidate.version>` on that detached worktree. It runs `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all`; when clean it returns { mutated: false, candidate, result: { invocation, outcome: "NO_CHANGE" } }. When dirty it runs `git add -A`, commits with fixed EXHARNESS_AGENT_TOOL author/committer env and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, reads the new 40-hex HEAD and returns { mutated: true, candidate: { id: candidate.id, version: newHead }, result: { invocation, outcome: "CANDIDATE_CREATED" } }. All git commands use spawn with argv and shell:false in workspace.root. A missing executable returns non-mutating TOOL_UNAVAILABLE. The strategy updates currentCandidate from every ACT result; TOOL_UNAVAILABLE stops without promotion. Otherwise it invokes every declared verification capability and EVALUATE for that candidate, then invokes PROMOTE only when evaluation is PASS and ACT mutated true. Failed verification feeds the next prompt; a non-mutating ACT sets attempt outcome NO_CHANGE (Core variation outcome may be SEARCH_STATE_CHANGED). After maxAttempts it returns EXHAUSTED. The agent message and exit code never affect PASS or PROMOTE.

D7 — objective.evaluate returns PASS only when Core-supplied verifications for the current candidate contain a PASS record for every declared verifier; tool claimedSuccess/finalMessage are stored in the attempt record only.

D8 — AGENT_TASK_V1 = { id, repositoryRoot, baseRevision (40-hex), prompt, verifications: non-empty [{ name, command, args, timeoutMs }] } validated before any process starts; verifier names are unique, commands are non-empty strings, args are string arrays, and timeoutMs values are positive integers. AGENT_SUPERVISED_RESULT_V1 = { taskId, tool, toolVersion, status ACCEPTED|EXHAUSTED|TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, attempts: [{ index, resume, outcome: CANDIDATE_CREATED|NO_CHANGE, exitCode, timedOut, durationMs, claimedSuccess, candidateSha, mutated, foldedAgentCommits, verification: [{ name, status, reason }], feedbackChars }], acceptedSha }.

D9 — bin/exharness-agent.mjs: `run --tool <codex|kiro|agy> --task <task.json> [--command <path>] [--max-attempts N] [--timeout-ms T] [--permission WORKSPACE_EDIT|FULL_AUTO]` prints AGENT_SUPERVISED_RESULT_V1; `probe` prints versions; `smoke --tool <t> [--command <path>]` creates a temp repo with one failing test and a one-line fix prompt, runs the supervised loop and prints the result, or prints SKIPPED with reason NOT_INSTALLED (executable missing) or TOOL_FAILED_BEFORE_EDIT (tool exited non-zero with no change on attempt 1, which is how a missing login or credential surfaces); --command replaces the adapter launch tuple while retaining its argument builder and result parser; a .mjs/.js path sets command = process.execPath and prefixArgs = [absolute path] as in D4 (used by tests); it never reports ACCEPTED without a passing verification.

D10 — Fake CLI fixture test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs selects behavior from env FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO: FIX_FIRST, FIX_AFTER_FEEDBACK (fixes only when its prompt contains the line `ExHarness verification failed:`), NEVER_FIX, CLAIM_SUCCESS_NO_EDIT, SELF_COMMIT, PARTIAL_THEN_FIX (unrelated edit first, real fix after feedback), AUTH_FAIL (exit non-zero without edits), HANG. It records its pid, spawned child pid for HANG, argv and stdin to a JSON file for assertions; HANG spawns a long-lived child so AT2 can verify tree termination. It answers versionArgs with `fake-agent <FAKE_AGENT_VERSION or 0.0.0>`, implements "fix" as `git apply <FAKE_AGENT_SOLUTION_PATCH>` in its cwd when that env var is set and otherwise writes the built-in fix of the AT3 fixture, and when invoked with codex-style argv emits a first JSONL line {"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"fake-<n>"}.

D11 — Evidence basis: executed probe shows all three CLIs installed with non-interactive, resume and permission flags; only codex has --json; no ExHarness code launches external agents; BB-066 names only OpenHands. Official Antigravity session documentation and the local help-only probe are recorded in cli-session-docs.md.
implementationSlices: S1 — CLI adapters [AT1]: implement D1-D3 and the D10 fake CLI fixture. AT1 unit tests assert exact first/resume argv and stdin for each tool and permission profile, sessionRef parsing and win32 executable resolution.
S2 — Process runner [AT2]: implement D4. AT2 tests launch the fake CLI to assert verbatim prompts, bounded output hashes, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, and HANG process-tree timeout.

S3 — Supervised loop [AT3]: implement D5-D8. AT3 tests use the fake CLI on temporary git repositories to assert ACT candidate identity, independent verification, bounded feedback/retry, no-change rejection, commit folding and source repository preservation.

S4 — CLI and Living docs [AT4]: implement D9. AT4 tests run and smoke with the fake CLI, including missing and unauthenticated tools. Write the Living docs and root scripts; run test:agent-tools, verify:current-docs and npm test.

negativeVerificationCases: A prompt containing shell metacharacters is received verbatim by the fake tool and never interpreted.
A missing tool executable yields TOOL_UNAVAILABLE and no attempt is recorded as ACCEPTED.
A hung tool invocation is killed at timeoutMs and its process tree is no longer alive.
A tool that exits 0 and claims success without editing is not ACCEPTED (NO_CHANGE).
A tool that never fixes the task ends EXHAUSTED after exactly maxAttempts with no PROMOTE.
A tool that commits on its own has its commits folded into exactly one candidate commit.
After each fake scenario, source repository HEAD, branch refs and porcelain status are unchanged by ExHarness workspace operations.
smoke with an unavailable tool prints SKIPPED and never ACCEPTED.
Any write to packages/core-harness, packages/oracle, packages/agentic-system or docs/blackboard fails scope verification.
The AUTH_FAIL fake exits non-zero without edits; smoke returns SKIPPED TOOL_FAILED_BEFORE_EDIT and never ACCEPTED.
